Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024
Kabc020370362022
 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
 Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru. (Scch-_25) 
 - : Present:- 
 Smt. Prakriti Kalyanpur, B.A(L),Ll.B., Ll.M. 
 Xxiii Additional Small Causes Judge, Bengaluru . 
 Dated This The 19th Day Of August 2024 
 Mvc No.7019/2022 
 PETITIONER: Mr. Suresha  S/o Lakkappa,
 Aged about 48 years,
 Lenkanahalli Gollarahatti,
 Tuylahalli Post,
 Mayasandra Hobli,
 Chandrashekarapura,
 Turuvekere Taluk,
 Tumkur District - 572 213. 
 (By Sri.Harisha S.K.,
 Advocate/s.)
 V/S  RESPONDENTS: 1. Sri. Shekaraiah  S/o Shivanna,
 R/o Belagarahalli at Post,
 Nonavinakere Hobli,
 Tiptur Taluk,
 Tumkur District.
 (RC owner of TATA ACE  Goods vehicle bearing  SCCH - 25 2 MVC No. 7019/2022  Reg.No.KA-44-6841)
 (Ex-parte)
 2. ICICI Lombard General  Ins. Co. Ltd.,
 #121, 'The Estate', 9th Floor,
 Dickenson Road,
 M.G.Road,
 Bangalore -560 042.
Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/
1  (Insurer of TATA ACE Goods vehicle  bearing Reg.No.KA-44-6841)
 Policy No.3003/232803429/00/B00  Valid from 23.11.2021 to 22.11.2022.
 (By Sri. Gururaj Salur,
 Advocate.)
 ......
 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 23.09.2022.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 23.09.2022 at about 5.45pm the petitioner and one Darshan were standing on the extreme left side of Yadiyur- Kallur cross Road along with a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-  SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 7019/2022 44-V-3802, near Lenkanahalli Gate, Mayasandra Hobli,
Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkur District, a TATA ACE Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-6841 came with high speed, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, all of a sudden came from Yadiyur side and dashed against the petitioner and said Darshan. Due to impact both petitioner and Darshan were knocked to the ground and sustained grievous head and bodily injuries. 
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident the petitioner and said Darshan were shifted to Adichunchanagairi Hospital, B.G.Nagar and admitted as an inpatient on 23.09.2022. However, said Darshan died in the hospital at about 10.15pm on the same day. During the examination of the petitioner, he has sustained Left Distal Humerus fracture, left shaft both bones of forearm fracture and other injuries, underwent surgeries and discharged on 13.10.2022 with an advice to take complete bed rest. So far he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 7019/2022 expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment etc., At the time of accident he was hale and healthy, doing Agriculture and Milk Vending business and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. Due to accidental injuries he lost his income. He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock. The accident caused due to the carelessness, rash and negligent driving by the driver of the TATA ACE Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 33-6841. The Turuvekere Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.217/2022 P/U/Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC. Therefore, the 1 st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/
2 compensation to him. Hence, this petition. 
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement. In spite of due service of summons the respondent No.1 did not appear hence placed exparte. 
5. The objection of the respondent No.2.
SCCH - 25 5 MVC No. 7019/2022 It has denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of the policy in favour of the Respondent No.1 in respect of the TATA ACE vehicle bearing KA-44-6841. The driver of the TATA Ace vehicle did not have valid and effective DL and also FC to ply the vehicle as on the date of accident. Further denied the nature of accident,
involvement of the vehicle in the accident. There is non- compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of the MV Act. Further, at the time of accident the petitioner was on a motorcycle without wearing safety headgear. It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident. It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate. Therefore,
prayed for dismissal of the petition against it. 
6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 23.09.2022 at 5.45pm due to rash and negligent driving of driver of TATA ACE Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-6841 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries? 
SCCH - 25 6 MVC No. 7019/2022 2. Whether the Petitioner he is entitled for Compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award? 
7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.10 and Exs.17 & 18. He has also got examined Mr. Govindaraju J. - MRO at Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandya as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.11 to P.14. Dr.Nagaraj B.N got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 & 16. On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf. 
8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record. 
The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decision:
ILR 2010 KAR 2439 : Sri. Subhash Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 7019/2022 Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/
3 9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  10. Issue No.1:- 
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-6841, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.5. He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination. During the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worthwhile is elicited to disprove that the accident caused due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. On the other side, the respondents did not examine any witness nor produced documents to show there was negligence on the part of the petitioner. 
11. As per FIR at Ex.P.1, it was registered on the next SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 7019/2022 day of the accident on the complaint of one Nagesh - eye witness. Ex . P.2 spot mahazar and sketch are in accordance with the statement given by the petitioner. The IMV report at Ex.P.4 also shows that the TATA ACE Goods vehicle was damaged to its front left side bumper assembly, front left side headlight assembly and front left side body sheet assembly damaged. The police have conducted investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P.5 against the driver of the TATA ACE Goods vehicle. The petitioner has also examined MRO of Aadhichunchanagiri Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.11 to 14, authorization letter, MLC Extract, police intimation and case sheet. During his cross examination, nothing worthwhile is elicited. The respondent No.2 has contended that the petitioner did not wear helmet as on the date of accident and there is sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself. Howevcer they have not led any evidence to prove the same. Therefore, on the basis of all these documents the tribunal holds that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA ACE Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44- SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 7019/2022 6841. Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative. 
12. Issue No.2:- 
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate at Ex.P.3. As per this document, the petitioner has suffered (i) Tenderness over the left shoulder, (ii) Tenderness over the left forearm, (iii) Tenderness over the left hand, swelling and (iv) Tenderness over the left upper arm. Out of these injuries, injury Nos.(ii) and (iv) are grievous in nature and rest are simple in nature. 
Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/
4 13. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 & 16 clinical examination note and X-ray film. He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed comminuted fracture of the left radius & distal ulna with distal humerus. 
He has further stated that the petitioner is suffering from disability of the left arm at 52% and to the whole body at 17%.
SCCH - 25 10 MVC No. 7019/2022 14. PW.3 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner. Further there is improvement in the muscle power, girth from the date of accident to date of assessment of disability. It is time for removal of implants. Injuries are healed. Fractures are united. Presently the petitioner is not under any treatment. After removal of implants the present complaints may vary. 
The petitioner can do his day today work with some difficulties. The petitioner is not using any external support for his hand. The petitioner does not suffer from any severe restrictions in the upper limb. The petitioner can do supervisory work. 
Disability:
15. From the evidence of PW.3 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered comminuted fracture of the left radius & distal ulna with distal humerus. The fractures are united with elbow stiffness. He has stated that he was working as an Agriculturist and was doing Milk Vending. This means he has to use his hand. This kind of SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 7019/2022 disability will affect his day to day work. Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 17%. 
Monthly income:
16. The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was doing Agriculture and Milk Vending business and earning Rs.25,000/- per month. In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like RTCs, Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings. The accident occurred in the year 2022. Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,500/-
per month. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 49 years as could be made out from Ex.P.7/Notarized copy of DL. He was hale and healthy before the accident. Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
 i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:- 
 After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Aadichunchanagiri Hospital wherein admitted and treated as an inpatient from 23.09.2022 to 13.10.2022 and was SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 7019/2022 diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.6/Discharge summary of Aadichunchanagiri Hospital. Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous and simple, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head. 
Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/
5 ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc. In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Exs.P.9 & 17 for a sum of Rs.28,158/- & Rs.15,380/- in total Rs.43,538/-. There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head. 
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries. The petitioner has produced discharge summary at Ex.P.6 of Aadichunchanagiri Hospital to show the SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 7019/2022 duration and treatment in the said hospital. Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him. Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,500/- under this head. 
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
The counsel for the Respondent No.2 relied on ILR 2010 KAR 2439 : Sri. Subhash Vs.
The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Wherein it is observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka that ' if the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise'. However in the case on hand, even if the petitioner has continued the Agricultural work it is clear from his evidence that the left hand has become useless and Agriculture requires lot of manual labor which can be done only if the both the hands and both the legs are normal. 
On perusal of Ex.P.7/Notarized copy of the petitioner, the petitioner's birth year is mentioned as 1973 and the accident SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 7019/2022 occurred on 23.09.2022. As such, petitioner's age is considered as 49 years. Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 49 years. As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 13. Therefore,
the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,11,060/- (Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 13 x 17%=
Rs.4,11,060/-) under this head. 
 (v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 49 years at the time of accident. He has sustained grievous and simple injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 17% functional disability. The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life. Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts. 
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered,
Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/
6 a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head. 
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES: 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above SCCH - 25 15 MVC No.
7019/2022 said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise. 
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head. 
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
As per the version of the PW.3, the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-. In this regard the petitioner or the PW.3 have not produced any estimation letter. Therefore,
looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries, evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head. 
17. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.60,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.43,538/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.15,500/-
period SCCH - 25 16 MVC No. 7019/2022 4. Loss of future income Rs.4,11,060/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.5,90,098/-
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.5,90,100/- and same is awarded under to the Petitioner. 
Liability Suresha vs Shekaraiah on 19 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37445310/
7 18. The Respondents did not prove their defence as discussed above. Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner. However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner. The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/-
but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,90,100/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 7019/2022 of petition till its realization. Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed. Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative. 
19. Issue No.3:- 
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER The petition is allowed in part with cost. The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,90,100/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Ninety Thousand and One Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner. 
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount SCCH - 25 18 MVC No. 7019/2022 with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award. 
On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner for a period of 3 years in any N/S Bank and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. Draw decree accordingly. 
(Dictated to the stenographer on line, revised, corrected and then pronounced in the open court this the 19th day of August 2024) (PRAKRITI KALYANPUR) XXIII ASCJ & ACJM, Bengaluru. 
ANNEXURE List of Witnesses examined for Petitioner:
PW.1 Mr. Suresha PW.2 Mr. Govindaraju J.
PW.3 Dr. Nagaraj B.N.

Ex. P1 True copy of FIR with complaint Ex.P2 True copy of Spot mahazar with  Sketch Ex.
